## **1. Creating the project**

First, I created a new **RStudio Project** for the assignment. This keeps all files in one place and makes version control easier because the project folder becomes the working directory.

Inside the project, I created a simple "example.qmd" file and knitted it to HTML to confirm that the file works correctly. This step is important because it checks that the Quarto document renders before I start tracking changes with Git.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
data <- read.csv("data/dataset.csv")
```
:::


## **2. Initialising Git and connect GitHub**

#### Next, I opened the terminal in the project folder and initialised Git using the following commands:

**- git init**

**- git status**

#### This creates a local repository so Git can track my changes. I then added the files and made the first commit:

**- git add .**

**- git commit -m "Initial commit with example qmd"**

#### After that, I created a new repository on GitHub and linked it to my local project:

**- git remote add origin https://github.com/adityasharma0404/ETC5513-AdityaSharma-Assignment2.git**

**- git branch -M main**

**- git push -u origin main**
